note: Design-space audit only; no balance or strength claim.

heroes.name: Bone
heroes.evidence: DataPiece uses compiled movement/attack; lifespan comes from config; no hero-specific override observed.

heroes.name: Ghoul
heroes.evidence: DataPiece uses compiled forward-cone movement/attack; forward orientation is declared in config.

heroes.name: Obelisk
heroes.evidence: DataPiece uses config-declared immobile movement and orthogonal attack.

heroes.name: Phantom
heroes.evidence: DataPiece uses config-declared knight geometry and spell classification; no Python override.

heroes.name: Sentry
heroes.evidence: DataPiece uses config-declared ray geometry and spell classification; no Python override.

heroes.name: FrostMage
heroes.evidence: Unique Nevada targeting/effect algorithm is specialized, but range=3, cross footprint and spell name are duplicated in Python while also declared in config.

heroes.name: Lich
heroes.evidence: Spawn validation is unique lifecycle logic; spawn_cooldown is read from config. Spawn direction and Ghoul result are rule-specific algorithmic semantics.

heroes.name: BoneLord
heroes.evidence: on_kill spawn-unit behavior is represented in config but requires specialized state-transition handling.

heroes.name: Ranger
heroes.evidence: DataPiece consumes config ray geometry, minimum range and spell classification.

heroes.name: Nightshade
heroes.evidence: DataPiece consumes config orthogonal range and ghost movement flag.

heroes.name: Templar
heroes.evidence: Reflect/redirect-damage passive is a state-transition mechanic; the passive metadata and cooldown are declared in config but resolution is specialized.

heroes.name: Berserker
heroes.evidence: on_attack area-damage passive is state-transition logic; config describes it but generic DataPiece movement does not implement the event effect.

heroes.name: Pyromancer
heroes.evidence: Ignite is unique spell resolution; Python hardcodes a 3-square neighborhood and spell name instead of reading equivalent geometry from config.

heroes.name: Dragoon
heroes.evidence: Jump is unique and specialized, but Python hardcodes the direction set and two-step midpoint semantics; jump_max is read from config.

heroes.name: Cleric
heroes.evidence: Purify is unique state-dependent spell logic; Python hardcodes a radius-2 scan and spell name although the active spell is declared in config.

heroes.name: Trickster
heroes.evidence: Swap is unique state-transition logic; Python hardcodes a radius-3 scan and spell name rather than consuming configurable range metadata.

heroes.name: Geomancer
heroes.evidence: Barricade is unique board-alteration logic; Python hardcodes the eight adjacent offsets and spell name while config only declares the spell.

heroes.name: Inquisitor
heroes.evidence: Aura is unique area/passive logic; aura_radius is correctly read from config, while the square-radius algorithm remains specialized.

heroes.name: StoneWall
heroes.evidence: DataPiece consumes config immobile/no-attack behavior and lifespan.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Specialized Python spell generators duplicate spell names and geometric ranges/patterns instead of deriving all reusable parameters from the declarative model.

The schema currently describes data but not the complete state-transition semantics for unique event-driven or board-altering mechanics; forcing these algorithms into JSON would be inappropriate without an expressive DSL contract.
A complete gameplay-vector audit requires valid reconstructed replay states and a versioned sampling protocol; the present artifact is intentionally design-vector only.

recommended_next_actions: Add generic schema fields only for repeated parameters proven across multiple specialized spell implementations.
Add regression tests before moving any duplicated parameter from Python into config.
Do not refactor unique algorithms into JSON solely to satisfy data-driven goals.
Implement gameplay-vector extraction as a separate evidence block after replay/state sampling contracts are frozen.
